items.title: Send these readings to your care team this week
items.text: Your average blood sugar was 198.1 mg/dL, which is higher than the target. Contact your care team this week to discuss your readings.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal may go with a smaller rise in blood sugar, especially if you walk for 10 to 19 minutes. If you take insulin or a sulfonylurea, ask your care team about low sugar before adding walks after meals.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Eating dinner at 8 pm or later may go with a rise in blood sugar, so try to start dinner before 8 pm. In the program, sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners than after earlier ones.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 11.2 hours, which is less than the 13 hours that may be beneficial. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points in the program.
